verdict.rationale: Convex documents self-hosting its open-source backend on your own servers, with Docker or a prebuilt binary, backed by storage such as Postgres, RDS, Neon or SQLite. That lets you decide where your data physically lives. The evidence never shows region or residency selection for the managed Convex cloud service, so data location is only controllable by taking on self-hosting. Missing for 10: region selection for cloud deployments, documented data-residency guarantees or a region list, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: you can run the Convex backend on your own servers. Self-hosted Convex runs the open-source backend, and contains the same fully up-to-date code the cloud service uses.
Self-hosted Convex works well with a variety of tools including Neon, Fly.io, Vercel, Netlify, RDS, Sqlite, Postgres, and more.
You can either use Docker (recommended) or a prebuilt binary to self host Convex.
